conbody.p: “Copyright trolling” is when holders vigilantly sue small infringements in order to get settlement money, prioritizing profit over fighting for the integrity of their creative works. One notable example of this abuse is the actions of Malibu Media, LLC. Malibu Media, an adult film producer, has garnered a reputation in the world of copyright law for trolling, using third party platforms to post their own content to torrent websites, tracking and trapping illegal downloaders. Malibu Media then sues individual IP addresses as a John Doe, subpoenaing internet service providers (ISPs) to reveal the identities behind each IP address. This practice, known as multiple defendant John Doe (MDJD) litigation, accounts for over 43% of copyright lawsuits filed in 2013, and has drastically increased since the 2000’s. Legal scholar, Matthew Sag explains it simply: The economic viability of MDJD litigation depends on suing as many defendants as possible in a single action to keep costs low and leveraging the threat of statutory damages in order to maximize the flow of settlement dollars.
